article_blocks.text: Strain Type: 85% indica / 15% sativa
Genetics: Crippled Rhino × Pit Bull
Breeder: Stoney Girl Gardens
THC Content: up to 32%
CBD Content: N/A
Terpene Profile: N/A
Primary Flavors: Chocolate, hash, sweet tropical fruit, lilac
Flowering Time (Indoor): Approximately 35–45 days
Outdoor Harvest Time: late September
Indoor Yield: approximately 5–9 ounces
Outdoor Yield: up to 8 pounds per large plant
Grow Difficulty: Intermediate

Crippled Pit comes from a period of marijuana breeding when exotic flavor did not automatically mean candy, sherbet, or dessert terpenes. Its personality reaches further back, drawing heavily on the Chocolate Thai character buried within its ancestry and combining it with the compact power of old-school indica breeding. Sweetness is present, but it arrives beside hash, flowers, earth, chocolate, and tropical notes rather than dominating them.

The plant can be equally unusual: very large leaves, tall branching, heavy resin development, dense elongated flowers, and a tendency to turn purple when exposed to cooler temperatures. Add an exceptionally short reported bloom cycle and a forceful, long-duration high, and this largely forgotten cultivar becomes an interesting piece of Pacific Northwest cannabis history rather than simply another obscure weed strain. Stoney Girl Gardens released Crippit to the cannabis community in 2008, and the strain was later featured in The Big Book of Buds Volume 4 .
Genetics and Lineage

The direct cross behind Crippled Pit is Crippled Rhino × Pit Bull, both associated with Stoney Girl Gardens’ Oregon breeding program. The breeder describes taking its Pit Bull to Crippled Rhino in an effort to retain the latter’s exotic Thai qualities while creating a plant better adapted to outdoor cultivation and considerably quicker to finish. That objective matters because Crippled Rhino carries old tropical ancestry that would normally suggest a much longer maturation period. In Crippit, those flavors survive inside a substantially faster indica-dominant framework.

Crippled Rhino adds another layer of depth to the pedigree. Current Stoney Girl Gardens material identifies that parent as White Rhino × Crippler, a pedigree also reflected in the Phylos genotype record for Stoney Girl Gardens’ Crippled Rhino. Its background carries Chocolate Thai influence, which explains why the breeder repeatedly emphasized an old-fashioned Thai or “Buddha stick” quality when discussing Crippit. Pit Bull provides the other half of the equation and belongs to Stoney Girl Gardens’ own breeding family, bringing additional indica influence, strength, and rapid maturation. The result was categorized by the breeder as roughly 85% indica and 15% sativa despite retaining surprisingly obvious tropical and Thai-like traits.

That ancestry also explains why the plant does not conform neatly to the stereotypical short, squat indica. Mature examples can stretch upward and branch heavily while carrying enormous, broad leaves. Archived breeder information describes a Christmas-tree or umbrella-style structure, multiple secondary colas, and unusually large flowers that can appear somewhat loose externally while remaining quite dense inside.
Effects and Experience

The experience begins with considerably more mental impact than the 85% indica classification might suggest. According to the original breeder description, the onset is immediate, euphoric, dreamy, cheerful, and unusually persistent. Instead of slowly building from the body upward, the initial change can feel cerebral first: ordinary thoughts become more abstract, mood rises, and attention may drift toward music, conversation, food, or whatever happens to occupy the moment. This quality helps explain why Stoney Girl Gardens also characterized it as enjoyable social or “party” cannabis despite its heavy genetic composition.

Physical relaxation becomes harder to ignore as the high matures. At moderate consumption levels, the mental component can remain active while muscular tension gives way to a warmer and more settled body sensation. Greater amounts are far more likely to reveal the cultivar’s indica foundation, creating pronounced heaviness and eventually couch-lock for some consumers. Because the historical breeder material claimed exceptionally high potency and modern secondary descriptions still place Crippled Pit firmly in high-THC territory, inexperienced consumers should approach it conservatively rather than treating its old-school pedigree as an indication of mild marijuana.

High-THC cannabis can also produce unwanted effects. NIDA notes that THC may alter perception, memory, judgment, coordination, and mood, while larger amounts or particularly potent products can increase the likelihood of anxiety, fear, distrust, or panic. Crippled Pit therefore makes considerably more sense when there are no driving responsibilities or tasks demanding precise concentration.
Medical Benefits

Stoney Girl Gardens historically positioned Crippit as medical marijuana for severe nausea, appetite problems, pain, chemotherapy-related symptoms, and evening relief, while also highlighting its upbeat mental character. Those breeder observations are useful for understanding how the cultivar was originally used, but they should not be confused with clinical evidence specific to Crippled Pit. No controlled clinical study has established this individual strain as a treatment for cancer, depression, glaucoma, PTSD, chronic pain , or another medical condition.

There is broader evidence that cannabinoids can affect symptoms relevant to some of those applications. NIDA notes that cannabis may help manage nausea and vomiting associated with chemotherapy and that increased appetite is a commonly observed effect of marijuana. Cannabis can also produce relaxation and substantial changes in pain perception, although response depends on THC concentration, dose, method of administration, previous experience, and individual physiology.

The distinction becomes especially important with potent flower. More THC does not necessarily mean better symptom control, and higher doses can increase undesirable cognitive or psychological effects. Anyone considering cannabis for persistent pain, chemotherapy symptoms, mood disorders, sleep difficulties, or another diagnosed condition should make treatment decisions with an appropriate healthcare professional rather than relying on the reputation of a strain alone.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Crippled Pit’s flavor is one of the clearest surviving links to its older genetics. Stoney Girl Gardens emphasized Chocolate Thai, lilac, hash, tropical sweetness, and an old Buddha-stick character, describing a profile that changes substantially after curing. Fresh flower may come across as sweet and floral first, while properly cured buds can expose deeper chocolate, earthy hash, and exotic tropical qualities inherited through the Crippled Rhino side.

There is no reliable public laboratory terpene analysis establishing a definitive dominant-terpene hierarchy for this cultivar. Assigning myrcene, caryophyllene, limonene, or another familiar compound simply from aroma would therefore create a level of certainty that the available evidence does not support. What can be documented is the breeder’s sensory profile: a Thai-oriented upper note, a sweeter tropical or Hawaiian-like foundation, restrained floral character, lilac, hash, and chocolate-like richness.

The cure deserves particular attention. Stoney Girl Gardens specifically observed that aging the harvested weed brought forward more of the exotic Chocolate Thai expression. Rather than smelling strongest immediately after drying, well-finished flowers can become darker and more complex with time, trading some green freshness for sweeter hash, cocoa, floral perfume, and an unusual tropical finish.
Growing Information

Despite being strongly indica-dominant, Crippled Pit can become a substantial plant. Breeder descriptions portray broad, thick fan leaves combined with a tall Christmas-tree or umbrella silhouette, vigorous side branching, and multiple productive secondary colas. Indoor examples were historically listed around six feet at maturity, while outdoor plants could become dramatically larger where unrestricted root space and a long vegetative season were available. Training early is therefore more useful than assuming the plant will remain short simply because of its indica percentage.

Its greatest cultivation curiosity is speed. Stoney Girl Gardens repeatedly described Crippit as capable of finishing in roughly six weeks, with archival entries ranging from approximately 35 to 45 days of bloom. That is unusually fast for marijuana carrying noticeable Thai influence. Growers should nevertheless use trichome development and flower maturity—not a calendar alone—to decide harvest timing, since environment and phenotype can shift the actual finish.

Late flowering can bring considerable visual change. Cooler conditions encourage green tissue to deepen toward purple, while resin may extend beyond the buds and onto the broad fan leaves. The flowers grow long and chunky and can become denser internally than their shape initially suggests, making airflow worthwhile as they mature. Historical breeder yield claims reached 5–9 ounces indoors and exceptionally large outdoor numbers, but those figures should be viewed as potential under favorable conditions rather than guaranteed production.
FAQ
What is Crippled Pit strain?
Crippled Pit, also called Crippit or Cripit, is an indica-dominant cannabis hybrid bred by Stoney Girl Gardens. The breeder identifies it as approximately 85% indica and 15% sativa.
What are the genetics of Crippled Pit?
The verified direct parents are Crippled Rhino × Pit Bull. Stoney Girl Gardens’ current material continues to describe Crippit as this same combination.
How strong is Crippled Pit?

Historical breeder material claimed THC reaching approximately 32%, while secondary strain references commonly give lower figures. Because cannabinoid concentration varies considerably between individual plants and harvests, a current laboratory certificate is more meaningful than a historical strain maximum.
What does Crippled Pit taste like?

Its old-school profile combines chocolate, tropical sweetness, hash, lilac, floral notes, and Thai-like spice. The breeder particularly emphasized the emergence of Chocolate Thai qualities after the flowers receive a proper cure.
How long does Crippled Pit take to flower?
Stoney Girl Gardens described an exceptionally rapid flowering period of roughly 35–45 days, often summarized as about six weeks. Actual harvest timing should still be determined by plant maturity.
Final Thoughts on Crippled Pit

Crippled Pit represents a style of cannabis breeding that feels increasingly uncommon. Instead of chasing maximum fruit sweetness or modern dessert flavors, Stoney Girl Gardens preserved an exotic Thai-influenced character inside a fast-finishing, heavily indica framework. Chocolate, lilac, hash, tropical sweetness, purple coloration, oversized leaves, and long-lasting intoxication give the cultivar an identity that is difficult to confuse with newer cookie- and candy-derived weed strains .

Its history may be the strongest reason the strain remains worth documenting. Released by Stoney Girl Gardens in 2008 and built from Crippled Rhino × Pit Bull, Crippit connects Oregon breeding with older White Rhino, Crippler, Pit Bull, and Chocolate Thai influences while accomplishing the unusual goal of bringing those flavors into a plant capable of finishing in roughly six weeks. For collectors and growers interested in cannabis genetics beyond today’s dominant commercial families, Crippled Pit remains a distinctive old-school hybrid with enough unusual flavor, structure, coloration, and potency to justify its place in a serious marijuana strain library.
